mechanics.mechanic: Open by defining the topic, clarifying what the discussion will and will not cover, and previewing the major categories, decision criteria, and practical outcomes.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the subject is broad, technical, or likely to create confusion about scope.
mechanics.avoid: Do not promise exhaustive coverage unless the structure can realistically support it; avoid listing topics without showing how they relate.

mechanics.mechanic: Identify a common label or assumption, explain why it is incomplete, and replace it with a more useful working definition before proceeding.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when everyday terminology groups together items with different purposes, risks, or mechanisms.
mechanics.avoid: Do not merely criticize the label; provide a clear alternative that improves the reader’s ability to reason about the subject.

mechanics.mechanic: Arrange options into layers, beginning with foundational behaviors or conditions and progressing toward more targeted or intensive interventions.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when choices differ in priority, dependency, or strength of effect.
mechanics.avoid: Do not imply that higher layers are universally superior; explain that later options depend on needs, context, and unresolved gaps.

mechanics.function: Turning advice into a decision framework
mechanics.mechanic: Replace a universal recommendation with a short sequence of diagnostic questions involving need, current outcomes, constraints, affordability, and alternatives.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the appropriate choice varies substantially between individuals.
mechanics.avoid: Do not present the questions as a substitute for professional evaluation when safety, diagnosis, or treatment decisions are involved.

mechanics.function: Separating foundational support from targeted effects
mechanics.mechanic: Distinguish broad, gap-filling measures from single-purpose interventions aimed at a defined outcome, then explain why each category may call for a different selection strategy.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when a product or intervention category contains both general-support and outcome-specific options.
mechanics.avoid: Do not blur prevention, correction of deficiency, enhancement, and treatment into one claim.

mechanics.mechanic: Move from the practical goal to the relevant system, then to the proposed mechanism, and finally to the decision implication.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when readers need enough biological or technical explanation to understand why an option might help.
mechanics.avoid: Do not introduce mechanistic detail that has no bearing on the decision, and do not treat a plausible mechanism as proof of effectiveness.

mechanics.mechanic: State the strongest version of a skeptical objection, acknowledge the circumstance in which it is valid, and then identify the narrower conditions under which the intervention may still be useful.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the topic has polarized opinions or when a simple criticism is partly correct but overgeneralized.
mechanics.avoid: Do not dismiss skeptics rhetorically or neutralize the objection with vague exceptions; specify the relevant conditions and limits.

mechanics.mechanic: Present a case in which the appropriate action is minimal or unnecessary, then contrast it with cases where a need is evident.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when readers may assume that every person should adopt the same protocol or solution.
mechanics.avoid: Do not use exceptional cases to undermine the general framework; make the decision boundary explicit.

mechanics.mechanic: Briefly restate the hierarchy, categories, or governing principles at transition points so the audience can integrate the accumulated structure before moving to details.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use after a long conceptual section or before shifting from general principles to specific applications.
mechanics.avoid: Do not repeat every example; recap the organizing logic rather than the full preceding discussion.

mechanics.function: Connecting recommendations to constraints and trade-offs
mechanics.mechanic: Evaluate an option not only by its potential benefit but also by cost, convenience, sourcing, timing, interactions, adherence, and opportunity cost.
mechanics.when_to_use: Use when the practical value of an intervention depends on more than efficacy alone.
mechanics.avoid: Do not imply that a more expensive, complex, or concentrated option is automatically higher quality.
